subject: Integrated observability handoff — runbooks, trace hooks & alert routing
messages:
From: Jin Park <jin.park@acmehealth.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Observability kickoff / handoff for Acme — dashboards + routing

Hey Avery and Marissa,

Thanks again for last week's demo. We're ready to move from trial to implementation and want to lock down the operational handoff so our SREs can run with the dashboards, tracing hooks, and alert flows. High-level asks from our side: 

- Verify the initial dashboard set (error rate, request latencies by route, token consumption per request).
- Confirm trace hook placement for the two critical services (payment-gateway, patient-lookup).
- Walk through an alert routing map and escalation for P0/P1 JVM OOM and model degradation.
- Provide a short runbook for on-call to follow during the first 72 hours after cutover.

Attached is our internal runbook excerpt and a CSV of our current alert triggers. We're aiming for a go-live window the week of June 7; happy to be flexible if Redwood needs more lead time.

Could you share a proposed cadence for the handoff (workshop, dry-run, go/no-go)? Also please confirm whether Redwood will subscribe these alerts to our PagerDuty instance or recommend a proxy routing approach.

Thanks,
Jin Park
SRE Lead — Acme Health
[Attachment: acme-runbook-excerpt.docx]

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Jin Park <jin.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff / handoff for Acme — dashboards + routing

Hi Jin — great to hear the momentum. Quick confirmation and proposed plan below.

Summary of what Redwood will deliver before the go-live window: 
- Dashboard pack: latency-by-route, token-consumption-by-model, error-taxonomy overview, top-traces for 95/99 pctl.
- Trace hooks: recommended insertion points and short code snippets for the two services you called out. We instrument at the request boundary and at model inference call so we capture queueing + generation latency.
- Alert routing: we'll provide an alert matrix (severity, symptom, suggested responder, PagerDuty routing key / webhook). For P0/P1 we recommend direct PagerDuty integration from Redwood; for noisy P2s we suggest a webhook to your aggregator.
- Runbooks: an Acme-specific runbook draft (PDF) and a short one-page play for the first 72 hours.

Proposed handoff cadence: 
1) Workshop (90m) — May 31 at 10:00 AM PT: go over dashboards and trace hook placement; devs and SREs attend.
2) Dry-run (60m) — June 3: simulate a model-degradation incident using replay logs.
3) Go/no-go sync (30m) — June 6: final checklist and cutover window confirmation.

Attachments: acme-observability-runbook-v0.9.pdf (draft), alert-matrix-acme.csv

Action items for us (will complete before May 31):
- Marissa: populate dashboard templates and share read-only views.
- Laura: prepare the PagerDuty integration guide and routing snippet.
- Avery: provide trace hook examples and the 72-hour playbook.

Let me know whether the May 31 10:00 slot works and who from Acme will join (SRE, on-call, and one dev).

Best,
Avery Johnson
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme-observability-runbook-v0.9.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jin Park <jin.park@acmehealth.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff / handoff for Acme — dashboards + routing

Jin / team — adding a few technical details ahead of the workshop so we can hit the ground running.

Trace hook notes (high level):
- Place synchronous tracing at the HTTP handler just before request validation and immediately after the model call returns. We send span tags: route, model_version, sequence_length, prompt_hash.
- For the Patient Lookup service add an out-of-band span that records cache-hits vs misses so we can correlate token cost spikes to cache behavior.
- We'll provide sample middleware for Node/Go/Python — the snippets are in the runbook PDF.

Dashboard and error taxonomy: 
- Error taxonomy will be split by class: validation (4xx), infra (5xx), model (nonsensical output/eval regression). Each class gets an owner and a follow-up checklist.
- We recommend two alert thresholds for model degradation: (1) automated quality regression (A/B score drop) -> P1 to ML team, (2) hard latency SLA breach (95p > X ms) -> P0 to on-call.

PagerDuty routing: Laura will attach the recommended rules; Redwood will forward P0/P1 to your primary PD service key, and we can mirror lower-severity alerts to a webhook for your internal triage tool.

I'll bring a draft incident play for the dry-run (June 3) that walks through detection -> mitigation -> rollback to fallback model.

--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: alert-matrix-acme.csv]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jin Park <jin.park@acmehealth.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff / handoff for Acme — dashboards + routing

Thanks all — looks good. Quick commercial & logistics notes for the record: 

- We'll reserve a Dedicated handoff slot for Acme the week of June 7; cost and SLA terms already in the portal (HS-4721).
- For the PagerDuty connection we'll need a short security checklist filled out by Acme's infra team (service account, least privilege key, allowed webhook IPs). Laura will send the checklist after the May 31 workshop.

Next steps (confirmed):
- Jin to confirm attendees for May 31 workshop (SRE + 1 dev + product owner).
- Redwood to share dashboard links and runbook PDF before the workshop.
- Dry-run on June 3 (Marissa to lead).

Ben Carter
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
